solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put off, with bombs laid? Resolute!

parts.note: to put off is to deter, discourage
an area with bombs laid in it is mined

explanation.surface: Someone deterred by a minefield, or else steeled by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute and determined are synonyms: both describe someone firmly set on a purpose.

clue.text: Beer or tea makers have dropped the first two jugs

indicators.note: the first two letters of the makers' name are dropped from its front

parts.note: brewers make beer, and tea is also brewed

explanation.surface: Brewery staff seem to have smashed a couple of pitchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have dropped the first two' removes BR from BREWERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed water jug, so ewers are jugs.

clue.text: A gentle eccentric, dignified and graceful

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A description of a mild, quirky person who carries themselves well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the letters of A GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes a stylish poise that is both dignified and graceful in manner.

clue.text: Honey from bee? Well, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Someone musing that honey does, after all, come from a bee.
explanation.walkthrough: MEL is Latin for honey, still met in old pharmacy and in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel is the Latin word for honey, used in pharmacy for honey preparations.

clue.text: Sadly admit none put up for post?

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or regrettably, so the letters come out in a sorry jumbled order

explanation.surface: A regretful admission that nobody was put forward for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges the letters of ADMIT NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nominated is to be proposed as a candidate for a position or office.

clue.text: Closely follow mother's principles

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Advice to stick to the values your mother taught you.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down as undeniably true by an authority.

clue.text: Turned up a copper in standard old money

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the whole built word is read from bottom to top
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone found a penny tucked among some old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' suits a down clue: the built STACUD is read from bottom to top. Cu is copper's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducats were gold or silver coins used across Europe in former centuries, so old currency.

clue.text: True about first half of semi being close again

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for true wraps around the other piece

parts.note: something true is real

indicators.note: first half of takes the opening two of the word's four letters

explanation.surface: A semi-detached house apparently genuinely closing up shop again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reseal something is to seal it shut once more after opening it.

clue.text: Monthly, perhaps, miners getting large bottle

parts.note: a monthly is one example of a magazine, a mag
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

explanation.surface: A monthly publication and coal miners joining forces over a big bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine or champagne bottle holding twice the standard amount.

clue.text: Huge land mass, like one close to Africa

parts.note: as can mean like, in the same way
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word, its last letter

explanation.surface: A geography note about a vast continent lying near Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like nearness, as in the surface, but it takes the final letter of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a huge expanse of land on the globe.

clue.text: Musical works about New Testament — a task unfinished

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a task is a job to be done

explanation.surface: Choral pieces based on the New Testament, a job left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantatas are vocal compositions with chorus and soloists, often on sacred texts.

clue.text: Raise a ring, ecstatic

parts.note: to cock is to raise or tilt up, as in cocking an eyebrow
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be holding up a ring, perhaps newly engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop is an idiom for being jubilant, crowing with delight.

clue.text: Protect piece oddly only appearing in verse

indicators.note: oddly only keeps just the letters in odd positions, the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A defensive part that shows up, strangely, only in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly only' takes the first, third, fifth letters and so on of PROTECT PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic describes something belonging to or expressed in poetry rather than prose.

clue.text: Took a pistol, cornering wild mammals

indicators.note: cornering means the words close around and trap the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A hunter took a gun and trapped some wild animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cornering' signals letters held within TOOK A PISTOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Okapis are forest-dwelling African animals related to the giraffe, so mammals.

clue.text: Songbird cut half of this fly

indicators.note: cut half of keeps only the front two of the word's four letters

parts.note: to fly is to rush, hurry

explanation.surface: A bird snapping a fly in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a family of singing birds, the song thrush being well known.

clue.text: Liqueur drunk at a fair

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on a sweet spirit at the funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is an almond- or fruit-flavoured sweet spirit drink.

clue.text: Boy clutching twisted ankle in English national park

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the boy's word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A lad hurts his ankle while out walking in the national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' makes AKELAN; 'clutching' holds it. Lakeland is the Lake District, a mountainous park in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lakeland is another name for the Lake District, the national park in Cumbria, England.

clue.text: Fiancée, finally, bound to run off secretly

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: An engaged woman who will in the end be sure to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry, fitting the fiancée of the surface.

clue.text: Record thanks at start of gym class

indicators.note: at start of places the thanks word in front of the class word

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
PE, physical education, is school gym class

explanation.surface: A recorded thank-you message at the beginning of a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks; PE is physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to record it on magnetic tape.

clue.text: Move stealthily from front of boat at length

parts.note: the prow is the front part of a boat

explanation.surface: Creeping along the length of a boat from its bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of boat' is a definition of PROW, not a pick of the first letter of boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move about quietly and furtively, like a hunting animal.

clue.text: Wide-sleeved garment in khaki — monochrome

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words that follow, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A fashion note on a loose robe in a single drab colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters running across KHAKI and MONOCHROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a long, loose Japanese robe with wide sleeves.

clue.text: Rubbish I used to kick?

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, meaning nonsense
one's own foot is what one kicks with

explanation.surface: Dismissing nonsense, then a riddle about the body part a kicker uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation scoffs at a claim as nonsense, while literally naming the limb a person kicks with.

clue.text: Staff removing the last of stacks

indicators.note: removing the last of drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: stacks, as in stacks of money, means many

explanation.surface: Workers clearing away the final pile in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last of stacks' looks like its S, but stacks means MANY, which loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To staff a post is to man it, provide the people to run it.

clue.text: Bedpan Alex ordered that can be enlarged

indicators.note: ordered means put in a fresh arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient named Alex requested a bedpan, an extendable one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges the letters of BEDPAN ALEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Expandable describes something able to be increased in size or extent.
